numbers.note: the person's standing default, ten diffusive times. assumptions.statement: One thousand tracers is a round ensemble that makes the statistics cheap and keeps the cube root exact at ten per edge. Nothing physical picks this number.

assumptions.statement: The fit window sits below the diffusive time so the free regime is what is sampled, at the same tenth of it revision 1 chose. The exact upper end is an estimate until A4 constrains it.
assumptions.falsifier: an A4 interval that excludes this value replaces it

assumptions.statement: A lag may span at most about a tenth of the record, so that every lag in the fit is determined by many displacements rather than by one. The vocabulary requires the window to satisfy this statistical bound as well as the physical one but deliberately fixes no fraction -- a number chosen in the contract would be a threshold nobody measured -- so the value is declared here and carried into the plan.
assumptions.falsifier: a weighted fit whose slope is unchanged when the longest lag is shortened retires this fraction

kb_refs.claim: The laboratory's ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius, read off a thermometer by the operator. It is a reading and not a setpoint, and it is the room's rather than the sample's -- which is what makes it an operator reading at E3 and not a calibration at E2.
There is no thermometer beside the sample. The only thermometer in the laboratory reads the room, so any temperature attributed to the sample is a room reading applied to it.

Sample temperature is not under control on this instrument. A temperature stage exists but has never been connected, so nothing actuates the sample temperature and there is no setpoint to appeal to: any temperature a plan uses is an ambient value of the room, not a commanded one.
The diffusive time is the time a sphere needs to diffuse its own diameter, and it sets the shortest record length from which a mean squared displacement can be read.
The particles in the bottle in use have a diameter of 5 micrometres, with a coefficient of variation no greater than 2 per cent, measured directly by the operator on 2026-09-19.

The expected translational diffusivity of a tracer sphere in a bulk fluid is the Stokes-Einstein value, k_B T over 3 pi eta d. It is a prediction from the viscosity, the temperature and the diameter, not a measurement of how the particles actually move.
Dynamic viscosity of pure water near 293 K is of order one millipascal second, and it changes by roughly two percent per kelvin in that neighbourhood.
